text:
ashwin: Quick check-in — ran a broad slab allocation sweep across A10/T4/L4/A100/H100. Got an odd regression on L4 when token_slab > 1536. p95 spiked ~18%.

maria: ugh. what changed in the heuristic? :thinking:

ashwin: Nothing upstream. This was just tuning batch-formation caps + slab sizing. Reproducer attached below (small snippet from profiler).

kevin: can you paste the kernel selection trace? curious if it's falling back to the generic kernel.

ashwin: sure — here's the kernel decision log for an affected trace:

```
[2026-03-18T12:02:41Z] model=redwood-7b variant=quantized: kernel_selector: trying best_fit for seq_len=512, tokens_in_batch=1800
[2026-03-18T12:02:41Z] kernel_selector: mismatch mem_estimate 3.7GB > card_free 3.5GB => fallthrough to fallback_kernel_v2
[2026-03-18T12:02:41Z] fallback_kernel_v2: slower attention path chosen, kv_cache_frag=27%, copy_ops=1.8x
[2026-03-18T12:02:41Z] perf: latency 176ms (baseline 150ms) p95 210ms
```

oliver: looks like KV fragmentation spikes when slab >1536 and kernel picks fallback. memory rounding + alignment quirks on L4?

maria: can you share the compare between slab=1536 vs 2048 p95/p50/cost tokens? also which batch-formation policy used (continuous vs hard-slice)?

ashwin: data snapshot:

```
config A: slab=1536, queue_policy=continuous, target_tokens_per_batch=1200
p50  = 132ms
p95  = 160ms
cpu offload = no
kv_frag = 12%

config B: slab=2048, queue_policy=continuous, target_tokens_per_batch=1600
p50 = 145ms
p95 = 188ms
cpu offload = no
kv_frag = 28%

cost delta ~ +6% tokens/sec drop
```

kevin: that kv_frag doubling is suspicious. Might be packing boundary interaction with the allocator. L4's preferred kernel seems much more sensitive to extra KV pages.

oliver: we saw similar in the A100 -> H100 kernel-fit sweep but less extreme. L4's memory allocator rounds up page blocks differently.

maria: actionables?

ashwin: proposed short plan:
1) roll slab cap back to 1536 for L4 on prod as a safety gate (canary rule)
2) instrument extra kernel selection telemetry for boundary cases (emit chosen_kernel, mem_est, frag_pct)
3) experiment with queue_policy = 'slot-greedy' that forces tighter packing and reduces partial KVs
4) micro-benchmark kernel with artificially fragmented KV layouts

kevin: +1 to 1 & 2. For 3, try target_tokens_per_batch lower (1100) with slab=2048 and see if packing fixes frag.

bench-bot: automated-run summary: (run-id: bk-4829999)
- card=L4
- workloads=redwood-7b,redwood-1.5b
- configs tested=6
- best safe config: slab=1536 continuous target=1200 p95=159ms
- worst reg config: slab=2048 continuous target=1600 p95=189ms

maria: ok let's gate the change. ashwin can you open a small rollout PR for L4 slab cap and the telemetry? how long to get telemetry in prod? ~1 day?

ashwin: I can get the telemetry out in ~6 hours dry-run, 24 hours safe prod push. PR in a bit.

oliver: FYI I have a kernel microbench harness already, will run fragged-KV patterns tonight and drop results in this thread.

kevin: also add a check in the scheduled analyzer to alert when kv_frag > 20% on a cardclass for >1 hour.

ashwin: good call — will add alert rule.

maria: thanks. if we see similar on T4 or A10 bump the slab cap conservatively but keep telemetry.

ashwin: noted. creating ticket and PR now. will post PR link here.

bench-bot: ticket created: INF-2319 "L4 slab cap rollback + kernel selection telemetry" by ashwin

ashwin: PR: https://git.redwood/inference/infra/changes/1234 — contains telemetry + canary config for L4 slab cap=1536

oliver: running microbench now, will paste abbreviated results if anything interesting.

ashwin: thanks all :+1:
